script.base: Market prices a one-score road win for Buffalo: implied BUF 26.8, NYJ 20.8, total 47.5, not a blowout and not a slog. Base flow is BUF leading by about a score into the second half while both offenses keep their week-1 identities — Buffalo mixing James Cook (13 carries, 44 yards) with Josh Allen's legs (11/35), the Jets staying run-heavy with Breece Hall (19/107) and Justin Fields (12/48) enough to stay in the game, and Garrett Wilson (9 targets, 95 yards) still getting the dog's pass volume. Pace is moderate; late BUF clock work lifts Cook's carries, and NYJ does not fully abandon the run unless the deficit gets large.
script.flip1: BUF scores early through Allen explosives (Keon Coleman had 11 targets, 112 yards, 132 air yards in week 1) and leads by 14+. Jets then abandon the run, Hall's carries die, Wilson's targets spike in catch-up, and Cook mops up late clock while Buffalo's WR air yards stall.
script.flip2: Hall and Fields gash a BUF run defense that allowed 8.21 YPC and 10 runs of 10+, with DT Ed Oliver out, and the Jets lead or tie. Buffalo then drops Cook's carries and airs it out to Coleman/Josh Palmer; the total pushes through 47.5 on explosives rather than a grind.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the card lost. Wilson finished under 95.5 because the Jets' 20-ish points came on the ground — Fields kept a double-digit rush share and Hall got the explosives against a bad BUF front — so Wilson saw 6 or 7 targets, the questionable BUF corners all played, and Reynolds' vacated targets split to Tyler Johnson and Ruckert instead of stacking on Wilson. Cook finished under 44.5 because the NYJ front that just allowed 2.84 YPC and zero 10-yard runs did it again, Tufele's absence changed nothing, and Allen kept 10-plus designed runs, leaving Cook at 12-13 carries around 3 YPC (about 36-42 yards). Separately, Hall over 107.5 was the matchup everyone wanted and still lost: 107.5 is exactly his 19-carry week, any dip to 14 carries or a Fields vulture of the long runs misses, and a two-score BUF lead (flip 1) kills the carry count even with Oliver out. That counter is at least as strong as the Hall read, so Hall is not a leg. Unknown MetLife weather can also take the under on both passing efficiency and the total.
slip_story: One story only: BUF leads but does not blow it out (implied 26.8-20.8). Favorite-runs-the-clock Cook rush over pairs with dog-throws Wilson rec over; they win together in the base script and in a mild BUF lead, and they both die if the Jets jump ahead and only run (flip 2). Do not add Hall rush over (needs NYJ to keep feeding him) or a total under, and do not add Coleman/Palmer overs (those need the shootout flip). No TD legs, no second market on either player, no price so no slip is actually placeable. Braelon, Ty Johnson, Tyler Johnson, Ruckert, and Shakir fail role, fluky-efficiency, or questionable-dependent tests and stay off.
